feedback.problem: The coefficient of ${x}^{7}y$ in the expansion of ${(x+2y)}^{8}$ is
feedback.worked_solution:
The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer $n,$ we have

 

$$
(a+b)^{n}=(\frac{n}{0}){a}^{n}{b}^{0}+(\frac{n}{1}){a}^{n-1}{b}^{1}+(\frac{n}{2}){a}^{n-2}{b}^{2}+⋯+(\frac{n}{n}){a}^{0}{b}^{n}.
$$

In the case of ${(x+2y)}^{8},$ we have $a=x,$ $b=2y,$ and $n=8.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x+2y)}^{8}=(\frac{8}{0}){x}^{8}(2y)^{0}+(\frac{8}{1}){x}^{8-1}(2y)^{1}+(\frac{8}{2}){x}^{8-2}(2y)^{2}+⋯+(\frac{8}{8}){x}^{8-8}(2y)^{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

From here, we see that the ${x}^{7}y$ term must be

$$
(\frac{8}{1}){x}^{8-1}(2y)^{1}.
$$

Simplifying this term, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{8}{1}){x}^{8-1}(2y)^{1} & =8{x}^{7}\cdot (2y) \\  & =16{x}^{7}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coefficient of ${x}^{7}y$ is $16.$
